methodology.comparison: Uncalibrated existing analytical model vs freshly executed pinned KAIST/ASTRA backend; not comparison against measured end-to-end inference.
methodology.workload: Llama 3.1 8B BF16 weights/activations and BF16 KV; colocated; one replica; PP1/EP1; one prefill chunk; max batched tokens 2048; no prefix sharing/offload.
methodology.throughput: Output tokens / earliest-arrival-to-last-completion window for both. Native total-clock throughput retained separately; includes control tail.
methodology.arrivals: Native requests arrive simultaneously. Analytical public schema requires positive rate; use maximum 10000 requests/s (0.1 ms spacing). Batch-four initial wait is 0.3 ms and mean formation delay 0.15 ms. Single-request cases match exactly. No production code patched.
methodology.hardware: Capacity and memory/link bandwidth units aligned. Link =16 GiB/s, latency=1000 ns. Compute efficiency=.65, memory efficiency=.8, generic vLLM factor/launch/tiling and cache assumptions retained without fitting.
methodology.software: RTXPRO6000 upstream profiles report vLLM0.28.0/CUDA13.0; RTX4090 vLLM0.19.0/CUDA12.8. Analytical vLLM factor is not version- or kernel-calibrated.
methodology.operator_comparison: First transformer block COMP_NODE costs in native prefill and first decode graphs vs matching nine analytical operators. COMP_NODE cost is whole profiled kernel elapsed time, including its internal memory effects; not arithmetic-only time. Embedding/final norm/head/communications excluded from matched block comparison, retained in end-to-end simulations.
methodology.scope: End-to-end differences include operator coverage, traffic/cache assumptions, scheduling and communication, not just max() overlap. This small suite is not a universal accuracy assessment. No energy comparison because accounting scopes differ. No model weights or hardware inference executed.
